oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply Tuesday, with Brent shedding 5.21% to $83.76 and WTI falling 4.21% to $79.13, as signals of U.S.-Iran de-escalation unwound the geopolitical risk premium that had driven a 14-16% monthly rally. The API reported a 3.296-million-barrel crude inventory build for the week ending July 24, adding bearish weight. Partially cushioning the drop, Houthi attacks remained active — Saudi Aramco shut its 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery after a strike on July 27, and conflict spread from Hormuz to the Red Sea. OPEC+ is reportedly planning one final September quota increase before pausing hikes through year-end, while a temporary U.S. easing of Russia oil sanctions and Iranian flows continuing through Hormuz despite Gulf neighbor export disruptions added to supply-side complexity. RBOB gasoline led losses at -5.69%, though refined-product tightness remains a structural undercurrent.
drivers: U.S.-Iran de-escalation signals triggered a sharp unwind of geopolitical risk premium across the crude complex
API crude inventory build of 3.296 million barrels for the week ending July 24 reinforced bearish supply narrative
Saudi Aramco's 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery shut after Houthi strike, keeping downside limited amid ongoing regional disruptions

gas.summary: Natural gas prices retreated on both sides of the Atlantic Tuesday. Henry Hub fell 3.18% to $2.679/MMBtu, extending a steep 17.08% one-month decline, pointing to ample domestic supply conditions. TTF slipped 3.01% to €56.5/MWh, though that still leaves European gas up an extraordinary 38.54% over the past month, reflecting lingering supply security concerns. On the demand side, a report indicated the EU could cut gas demand by a quarter by 2030 if it meets its heat pump, solar, and wind targets, a longer-term bearish structural signal for LNG imports. Separately, escalating anti-government protests in Libya raised near-term supply risk for Mediterranean gas flows. Headline flow on gas was limited today; the divergence between a weak Henry Hub and elevated TTF remains the defining cross-market theme.
drivers: Henry Hub continues its monthly slide (-17.08%) on ample U.S. supply, while TTF remains elevated (+38.54% on the month) reflecting European supply security concerns
EU renewables report signals potential 25% gas demand reduction by 2030 if installation targets are met, a long-term bearish structural signal
Escalating protests in Libya introduce near-term upside risk to Mediterranean gas supply disruptions

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs were essentially flat at $77.99/EUA (+0.01%), with the weekly and monthly moves subdued (+4.19% on the month) despite highly volatile underlying energy prices. The main structural narrative was bearish for long-run gas-to-power demand: a report projected that meeting EU renewables targets could slash gas demand by a quarter by 2030. On the geopolitical side, a drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant was cited as briefly lifting oil to a two-week high earlier in the week, underscoring infrastructure vulnerability. Tata Power announced plans for India's first private nuclear plant by 2032 as India opens its civil nuclear sector. A new solar cell design was reported to address a longstanding efficiency degradation problem. Carbon price stability amid volatile gas suggests the market is balancing near-term fuel-switching signals against longer-term clean energy displacement expectations.
drivers: EU EUAs near flat on the day; carbon market appears to be balancing near-term fuel-switching demand against longer-run renewables displacement
Drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant highlighted critical power infrastructure vulnerability in the Gulf conflict zone
EU renewables report and new solar cell design advance reinforce a longer-term structural shift away from gas-fired generation
